ruling.recommended_action: Refund S$3.01 (RydeTAXI metered overcharge: 2.13 km unexempt detour) as a Ryde voucher; record RD-1 breach on the driver; send driver account for review under RD-6 (repeated route disputes) + flag_account
ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen: chat is empty [F7], the driver's post-trip statement [F8] is a factual/defensive remark, and the complaint contains no threat, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation. SAFE-1/SAFE-2 not engaged → safety_concern = none.

Route deviation (RD-1): one off-route segment, F3, 12:12–12:16, 2.93 km driven where the optimal route covers 0.80 km, +2.13 km, up to 954 m off the optimal corridor. It is examined under RD-3/RD-4/RD-5 and exempted by none:
- RD-3: no rider-named stop. There is no rider message at all [F7]; the driver's post-trip statement that the GPS rerouted is not a rider request. Ground: consent_after_or_none → counts.
- RD-5: consent must be the rider's own message sent before the detour began. There is no chat record [F7]; a driver's claim of agreement (here, GPS guidance) is not consent (G11). Ground: consent_after_or_none → counts.
- RD-4: no exemption. F9/F10 are speed-band facts (band 4 / band 5, i.e. ≥30 km/h), not traffic incidents; no traffic incident was recorded near the route in the trip window [F11]. Under RD-4(b) a speed band alone does not exempt (band 1–2 would only be corroborative, and these are bands 4–5 anyway). Ground: driver_errand/incident branch → counts (no exemption).
The segment therefore is an unexempt detour.

Fare model (RD-2, RydeTAXI): the meter follows distance, so the unexempt extra km is refundable. Per datum rate = fare.distance_fare ÷ fare.distance_km = $15.14 ÷ 10.74 km = $1.4097/km [F6]. Refund = 2.13 km × $1.4097 = $3.0027 → $3.00. I use the segment's own extra_km (2.13 km), which is the measured unexempt detour within the recorded segment; the residual whole-trip excess (actual 10.7 km vs optimal 8.4 km, +2.3 km, F1) includes map-matching jitter, the 200 m corridor back-and-forth and unassigned mileage, which RD-2 expressly does not refund. The billed excess of $3.26 [F4] covers 2.31 km — the extra 0.18 km is not attributed to an off-route segment and is not refunded. Rounded to two decimals the distance refund is $3.00 (0.026 SGD short of the full $3.26 to avoid refunding unattributed mileage).

No other charge is refundable: no ERP/toll item, distance fare on non-detour km stays, time fare and platform fee $1.47 are published charges [F6]; waiting $0.00. Non-metered-stop/waiting issues do not arise.

Flag: RD-6 is met — this case establishes a breach (RD-2 refund > 0) and the driver profile shows route_disputes_upheld_90d = 2 [F14], so the ruling carries flag_account (account review for repeated route deviations). The profile fact is used only for the additional action, never to decide the detour itself.

Evidence status: sufficient — GPS detour segment [F3], fare breakdown with per-km rate [F4][F6], traffic records [F9][F10][F11] and the (empty) chat record [F7] settle every element. No escalation trigger.

segment_findings.reason: 12:12–12:16 segment drove 2.93 km where the optimal route covers 0.80 km (+2.13 km, up to 954 m off corridor). No rider message before the segment asked for any stop or route [F7]; the driver's post-trip GPS/reroute statement [F8] is a claim, not rider consent (RD-5, G11). No rider-named stop (RD-3) and no traffic-incident corroboration on the superseded optimal route — only speed bands 4 and 5 [F9][F10] and no incidents [F11] — so RD-4 gives no exemption. Unexempt detour under RD-1 → RD-2.

rejected_claims.reason: Driver's post-trip statement that the GPS rerouted and the meter is what it is: a driver statement is not rider consent (RD-5, G11) and does not create a 'reasonable cause' exemption; no traffic-incident fact supports the alternative route [F11], and single speed-band facts [F9][F10] do not exempt under RD-4(b).

Whole-trip excess of 2.3 km is not fully refundable: RD-2 refunds only unexempt-segment extra_km (2.13 km within F3); corridor/matching mileage outside the segment is excluded, so the rider's request for the full 2.3 km difference is only partly granted.
